title: Learning: The Borrowed Key
text: A change is merged, built, signed and published. Who approved it, and who signed the result?
held: Two people stood behind the change, and the pipeline (not a person) signed the build.

cards.label: Refuse to build
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: reviewed by
fields.ok: Approved by a second maintainer before merge.

intrusion.detail: No review. The change was pushed directly to the release branch.
intrusion.why: Unreviewed code on the release branch means one stolen account can ship anything.
intrusion.reveal: The change reached main without anyone reviewing it.

temptations.label: Reuse the build cache from a fork to save ten minutes
temptations.why: A cache written by a fork is input from outside the project. A poisoned cache puts someone else's code into your artifact.

cards.label: Reject the upload
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: signed by
fields.ok: Signed by the pipeline's workload identity, with a short-lived certificate.

intrusion.detail: Signed with a personal key, from a laptop.
intrusion.why: A personal key can sign anything from anywhere. Releases are signed by the pipeline so the signature means “built here”.
intrusion.reveal: The artifact was signed with a developer's personal key instead of the pipeline's identity.

cards.label: Deploy the hotfix image a teammate built locally: it has the same fix
cards.why: The same fix is a claim. The local image has no review, no provenance and no pipeline signature behind it.

fields.label: policy
fields.value: built by the pipeline, from main, reviewed

teaches: Two-person review means no single account can ship code alone.
The pipeline signs releases, with an identity that can't leave the pipeline. A person's key proves only that a person signed.
Shared caches and local builds are inputs nobody reviewed.
